figure: Figure 9.1 — Ring traffic and directional bandwidth
issue: The figure note says 'no offload, latency or overlap', but the plotted 544 ms value depends on concurrent send and receive (overlap of the two directions). The note can therefore be read as contradicting the model used to produce the curve.
evidence: Caption: 'Each rank sends 1.75 times the logical tensor size and receives the same amount. Curves use 450 GB/s ...'. Prose on printed p. 156: 'With concurrent send and receive, its ideal time is T_ring ≈ 245/450 ≈ 0.54 s. Equivalently, 490 GB of sent-plus-received traffic divided by 900 GB/s gives the same time.' Figure note: 'Analytical model; no offload, latency or overlap; not measured.' If 'overlap' meant no send/receive overlap, the time would be 490/450 ≈ 1.09 s, not 0.54 s.
acceptance_test: Revise the note to say 'no offload, latency, or communication/computation overlap' (or equivalent), so it cannot be read as denying the concurrent send/receive assumption behind the plotted times.

figure: Figure 9.1 — Ring traffic and directional bandwidth
issue: The caption does not state the time formula used for the curves. A reader can see 'sent bytes per rank = 1.75 × tensor bytes' and 'ideal ring completion time' but is not told that the plotted time is sent bytes per rank divided by directional bandwidth, with send and receive concurrent.
evidence: Subtitle: 'sent bytes per rank = 1.75 × tensor bytes'. Caption: 'Each rank sends 1.75 times the logical tensor size and receives the same amount. Curves use 450 GB/s ...'. The caption never says 'time = sent bytes per rank / directional bandwidth' or 'assuming concurrent send and receive'. The prose on p. 156 supplies this, but the figure caption should be self-contained.
acceptance_test: Add one clause to the caption: 'Plotted time is sent bytes per rank divided by directional bandwidth, assuming concurrent send and receive.'

issue: The figure says 'Balanced ring neighbor order (both phases)' and shows R0→R1→R2→R3→R0, but it does not show which 2 B chunk each rank sends in each round. For a reader trying to reconstruct the ring algorithm, the diagram shows the neighbor order but not the chunk rotation that makes reduce-scatter and all-gather work.
evidence: Figure text: 'Balanced ring neighbor order (both phases)' with R0→R1→R2→R3→R0. Below: 'Each round sends one 2 B chunk to the next rank.' The figure does not label the chunks (e.g., chunk 0, chunk 1, chunk 2, chunk 3) or show which chunk moves in round 1, 2, 3. The caption says 'Reduce-scatter leaves one reduced element per rank; all-gather then replicates the already-reduced fragments', but the chunk rotation is left implicit.
acceptance_test: Either add small chunk labels (0/1/2/3) to the ring arrows or add one sentence to the caption: 'In round r, rank i sends chunk (i−r) mod N; the same rotation is used in both phases.'

figure: Figure 9.3 — The payload path is not the bootstrap path
issue: The figure's right-hand path places 'Plugin: MPI or OFI' under '3 Device runtime plus transport', while the bottom note says 'GPU-aware MPI can carry payload too; MPI is not CPU-only.' The diagram therefore shows MPI in two different roles (setup/control and transport/plugin) without visually distinguishing those roles.
evidence: Top dashed box: 'Launcher, rank/device mapping, rendezvous' with 'MPI or a store can distribute communicator IDs.' Right path under '3 Device runtime plus transport': 'SYCL / Level Zero path / Plugin: MPI or OFI / Actual path depends on build'. Bottom note: 'GPU-aware MPI can carry payload too; MPI is not CPU-only.' Caption: 'Dashed setup connections do not imply that MPI carries the collective payload; GPU-aware MPI is also a possible payload implementation.' The figure uses the same word 'MPI' for setup and for a possible transport/plugin without a visual or textual role distinction.
acceptance_test: Either label the right-path MPI entry as 'MPI transport (payload-capable)' or add a caption sentence: 'MPI appears in two roles: setup/rendezvous (dashed) and, in some builds, payload transport (solid); the figure does not imply they are the same path.'
